title: Use a district tile map to show every House seat as one square, with party told by panel.
rule: Give each district one square of the same size on a layout that keeps states in their places and districts in their order, with lines between states and each state’s code where its block leaves room. Set party and margin in one panel for each party, as Rule 14.7 sets seats on a map. Mark a seat unopposed on the ballot with a dot and a race decided another way with a ring, and name those seats in a note where the squares grow too small for the marks (Rule 14.12).
use_when: The reader asks which party won each House seat and by how much, and every seat should count the same.

use_instead.when: One state’s districts on their real shapes
How far each state moved, with direction

text: On a map of real districts, a few large rural seats fill the page while dozens of city seats shrink to dots. Equal squares give every seat the weight it has in the House, and the panels show each party’s seats without a party color.
why.basis: Design judgment, from the chart system our founder and editor approved in November 2026

builders: Form district-tile-map: node work/build/chart-kit/oa-chart.mjs build s82; encode state, district, party, cls, mark, col and row, all in clerk-house-results-2024-classes, which cartographer_round3_derive.py writes from the Clerk’s results and our own tile layout built from the Census Bureau’s district centers; table.group groups the table by state.
